thread:
alex.k: Heads-up — I pushed an RFC draft for the Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, quantization). Looking for quick triage and edge-case calls before we send to product for scope decisions.

marta: link? where'd you put it?

alex.k: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/optimize-recs-draft.md — top section is goals + non-goals, then per-workload recs.

ben: skimmed. big +1 on separating latency-sensitive vs throughput workloads. two quick asks: 1) add acceptance criteria for regressions, and 2) spell out KV-cache invalidation behavior for user-level pinning.

liz: also need to call out multi-tenant implications for Dedicated. caching recommendations can't assume single-tenant KV.

ajay: agree. quantization recs: are we recommending 4-bit quant only for non-critical outputs? need clarity on accuracy tradeoffs and fallback.

alex.k: good points. I added an "Acceptance & Rollout" section but it's terse. thinking of adding a small matrix: workload type x metric (p50, p95 latency, token-cost, quality-delta) + pass/fail thresholds. example: 

```
Acceptance matrix (example):
- latency-sensitive: p95 <= baseline * 1.1, quality-delta <= 1% deter.
- throughput-batch: tokens/sec >= baseline * 1.25, cost/token <= baseline * 0.85
- quantization (4-bit): downstream eval metrics (BLEU/EMB sim) within 2% of baseline
```

marta: put that in, but include how we measure "quality-delta" — eval suite vs production A/B? we should prefer eval + canary guardrails.

sam: infra-bot triggered: deploy-preview build #231 for rfc is ready at https://deploys/redwood/231 (test vectors included).

product-lead: we have 3 enterprise customers asking for stronger guidance on quantization safety and deterministic fallbacks. please flag any changes that would require contract/SLA negotiation.

ben: edge-case list I'm worried about: very long context windows (8k+), prompt-prefix caching correctness with streamed generation, and mixed-precision hardware (TF32/AMP) interactions with our kernel choices. add small experiments to measure KL divergence on long-tail prompts.

ajay: on hardware: recommend a section mapping quantization presets -> supported hardware with a fallback plan. e.g., if a server doesn't support fast int8 kernels, we fallback to slow fp16 with capacity gating.

alex.k: noted. I'll update RFC: add explicit experiments, acceptance matrix + measurement plan, and a compatibility table mapping quant presets to kernel support. also add a paragraph on privacy: cache TTLs per customer, and opt-out flags for embeddings.

liz: for Dedicated customers we should expose a toggle for per-customer cache partitioning in the Console and an opt-out API. also document migration steps.

product-lead: timeline? if we want to include this in next quarter roadmap, need final RFC by EOW and acceptance tests by mid-next-week. can eng commit to that?

alex.k: aiming for final RFC by Friday (EOW). acceptance test harness baseline runs are scheduled tomorrow.

sam: running baseline infra tests now, will share results in a follow-up thread.

marta: I'll add the eval suite definitions + sample prompts (latency-sensitive, retrieval-augmented, long-context adversarial).

ben: quick nit: include a short 'How to revert' section with config flags and monitoring alerts. very helpful during canary.

alex.k: done — will update and ping once RFC is revised. thanks for fast feedback :thumbsup:

infra-bot: status update queued: baseline tests 0/3 complete, will post artifacts to the RFC page when done.

alex.k: tagging @product-lead once RFC is finalized for scope decision.

product-lead: thanks everyone. expecting the updated doc and the acceptance matrix. if anything increases compliance scope (KMS/HSM) flag it ASAP.

sam: baseline run finished: artifacts https://artifacts/internal/optimize-baseline/231 — perf + quality csvs attached.

alex.k: received. I'll fold the artifact links into the RFC and raise a short PR for review.

marta: LGTM on plan, will review the final draft Thursday AM.

ben: will prepare a short regression checklist for the on-call playbook.

alex.k: thanks all — closing this thread once RFC PR is up.
